page: Microsoft Azure E32d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. It features an x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled, supplying two threads per core. Memory configuration includes 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Storage consists of 1288 GB of local SSD capacity bundled directly with the virtual machine, delivering fast local scratch space. There are zero discrete GPUs attached to this instance, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided. Synthetic benchmarks reflect consistent middle-tier compute across both single-threaded and multi-threaded suites, including a PassMark CPU score of 36,908.39, a Geekbench single-core score of 1,633.0, and a multi-core score of 13,826.0. Memory subsystem testing shows upper-tier throughput, highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score of 2,756.95 and an uncached large-block read bandwidth of 148.27 GB/sec.

Workload evaluation shows balanced performance across data processing and memory tasks, reaching 31.39 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 33.91 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound LLM execution remains competent for smaller models, achieving 280.92 tokens per second on text generation with a 135M parameter model, though throughput drops significantly on larger architectures due to the lack of dedicated acceleration. Cost efficiency is characterized by high density of RAM and integrated high-speed local disk capacity per compute thread. The instance is suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, distributed analytics nodes, and data-intensive business applications.

The x86_64 processor includes AVX-512 vector extensions and 48 MB of L3 cache, backed by Microsoft Hyper-V. In benchmark evaluations, the instance registers strong memory subsystem performance alongside reliable mid-tier CPU throughput, achieving 31.39 million Redis SET operations per second and 148.27 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Lacking dedicated GPUs, CPU-based LLM inference is limited to smaller parameter models. The bundled local storage and high RAM allocation make the E32d_v5 suited for large-scale enterprise databases, memory-resident data caches, real-time analytics, and heavy business processing workloads.
